:::{#exr-prediction-error}
#### Expected squared error from three sources

A prediction $\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}$ at a new point $\predvar_0$ has
squared bias $[\bias{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}}]^2 = 1$
and variance $\Var{\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}} = 2$.
The new response is $\Outvar_0 = \targetfnf{\predvar_0} + \noise$,
where $\noise$ has mean $0$ and variance $\varpar = 3$
and is independent of $\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}$.

1. What is the expected squared prediction error $\E{(\Outvar_0 - \etargetfnf{\predvar_0})^2}$?
2. If we could remove all bias and all variance of $\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}$,
   what would the expected squared prediction error be?
3. Which of the three quantities
   (squared bias, variance of $\etargetfnf{\predvar_0}$, $\varpar$)
   can a better prediction method reduce,
   and which cannot?

:::
